title: Optimizing Uncertainty Estimation on Scientific Visualizations Using Learning Models
problem: Deep learning models exhibit undue confidence on out-of-distribution inputs, leading to high-confidence misclassifications. The paper addresses this by enabling uncertainty quantification and selective classification.
motivation: Trustworthy uncertainty estimates are critical for deploying deep learning models in real-world industrial applications where incorrect high-confidence predictions can have serious consequences.
method: The approach changes deep learning models so they output not just a single prediction, but a full distribution showing how likely each possible answer is—revealing how confident the model really is. When confidence is too low, the model can choose to abstain (decline to predict) rather than guessing. The researchers tested this on three tasks: predicting air pressure and velocity around airplane wings using RANS simulations, classifying images in ImageNet1K, and recognizing MNIST handwritten digits.
key_novelty: Instead of making a confident guess, deep learning models output their full uncertainty about each possible answer and can choose to skip predictions when they're not confident enough.
contributions: Framework for uncertainty quantification in deep learning models for scientific visualization
Enables selective classification where models abstain on high-uncertainty predictions
Outputs prediction distributions instead of single predictions for informed decision-making
Comprehensive evaluation across computational fluid dynamics and computer vision tasks
primary_theme: uncertainty-aware deep learning for scientific visualization
